literal: He once composed the rhapsody "Observing My Life," its writing clear and far-reaching; its words say:
idiomatic: He once wrote the rhapsody Observing My Life, its language clear and far-reaching; it begins:

literal: Looking up at the distant clarity floating above, looking down at the deep mystery sinking below.
idiomatic: I lift my gaze to the far floating clarity above; I bend my eyes to the deep, sunken mystery below.

literal: Having raised the people, he established teaching; thus stewards divided the realms.
idiomatic: Once the people were raised, teaching was set; stewards of the land were appointed to divide the realms.

literal: Within were the various Xia, without were the barbarians; swiftly they passed through the Five Emperors and raced the Three Kings.
idiomatic: Within lay the myriad Xia; without, the barbarian tribes—racing through the Five Emperors, galloping past the Three Kings.

literal: The Great Way withdrew and the sun hid, "Minor Odes" was shattered and thus perished.
idiomatic: The Great Way withdrew and the sun went into hiding; the Minor Odes were shattered, and so it perished.

literal: Mourning the crimes of Zhao Wu, marveling at the ill fortune of Han Ling.
idiomatic: I mourn the crimes of Zhao Wu; I marvel at the ill fortune of Han Ling.

literal: The Bushel star toyed with the golden tripod, the Hall of Wu lost its pearl pouch.
idiomatic: The Bushel star played with the golden tripod; the Hall of Wu lost its pearl pouch.

literal: Chan and Jian waters curled into desert, Sacred Splendor extinguished into dragon wilderness.
idiomatic: The Chan and Jian streams curled into desert; Sacred Splendor was extinguished into dragon wilderness.

literal: Thus our king moved east; thus our ancestor flew south.
idiomatic: Thus our king moved east; thus our ancestor flew south.

literal: (Jin Central Banner as Langye prince crossed south; Zhitui was a Langye man, hence "our king.")
idiomatic: (The Jin Central Banner, as Prince of Langye, crossed south; Zhitui was a man of Langye, hence "our king.")

literal: Leaving Langye's migration to Yue, dwelling in Jinling's old statutes.
idiomatic: We left Langye's flight to Yue and made our home in Jinling's old statutes.

literal: Making feathered standards in the new capital, planting catalpa and nan in the water country.
idiomatic: We raised feathered standards in the new capital and planted catalpa and nan in the water country.

literal: Transmitting purity without decline, holding to law without forgetting.
idiomatic: We transmitted purity without decline and held to law without forgetting.

literal: Reaching my slight self's ninth generation, the declining age's accumulated fragrance of merit.
idiomatic: It reached my slight self in the ninth generation—the declining age's accumulated fragrance of merit.

literal: I asked where my good days had gone; the bell had grown weary of Liang.
idiomatic: I asked where my good days had gone; the bell had grown weary of Liang.

literal: Raising Fu Yi's flying beast,
idiomatic: They raised Fu Yi's flying beast,

literal: (Emperor Wu of Liang took in the fugitive Hou Jing and entrusted him with command; thus the foundation of rebellion was laid.)
idiomatic: (Emperor Wu of Liang took in the fugitive Hou Jing and gave him command—thus the foundation of rebellion was laid.)

literal: and the son, a wolf of greedy heart.
idiomatic: and the son—a wolf of greedy heart.

literal: (At first Emperor Wu raised Linchuan prince Zhengde as heir; after Zhaoming was born, Zhengde was returned to his original status and specially enfeoffed as Prince of Linhe.)
idiomatic: (At first Emperor Wu raised Linchuan prince Zhengde as heir; after Zhaoming was born, Zhengde was returned to his original status and specially enfeoffed as Prince of Linhe.)

literal: He still harbored resentment.
idiomatic: He still harbored resentment.

literal: He fled straight north and returned, amassed wealth and nurtured soldiers, and always harbored strange designs.
idiomatic: He fled straight to the north and returned, amassed wealth and nurtured soldiers, and always harbored strange designs.

literal: At first he summoned disaster from the outer marches; again he raised strife within the palace walls.
idiomatic: At first he summoned disaster from the outer marches; again he raised strife within the palace walls.

literal: (Zhengde requested to campaign against Hou Jing; reaching Xinlin, he rebelled and threw himself on Jing, who set him up as ruler to attack the Terrace City.)
idiomatic: (Zhengde requested to campaign against Hou Jing; reaching Xinlin, he rebelled and threw himself on Jing, who set him up as ruler to attack the Terrace City.)

literal: Though ten thousand li made a barrier, a single reed could still be sailed.
idiomatic: Though ten thousand li made a barrier, a single reed could still be sailed.

literal: They pointed their long spears at the golden towers and turned their bows toward the royal road.
idiomatic: They pointed their long spears at the golden towers and turned their bows toward the royal road.

literal: Those who came to rescue the throne exceeded a hundred thousand, yet not one knew how to seize the throat.
idiomatic: Those who came to rescue the throne exceeded a hundred thousand, yet not one knew how to seize the throat.

literal: Alas—the backbones of generals and ministers all bent their bodies before dogs and goats.
idiomatic: Alas—the backbones of generals and ministers all bent their bodies before dogs and goats.

literal: When the Terrace City fell, the relief armies alike inquired after the Two Palaces and paid homage to Hou Jing.
idiomatic: When the Terrace City fell, the relief armies alike inquired after the Two Palaces and paid homage to Hou Jing.

literal: The Martial Emperor suddenly grew weary of the world; the white sun dimmed and lost its light.
idiomatic: The Martial Emperor suddenly grew weary of the world; the white sun dimmed and lost its light.

literal: Having enjoyed the state for fifty years, how could its end not be unpeaceful?
idiomatic: Having enjoyed the state for fifty years, how could its end not be unpeaceful?

literal: The heir listened to the great villain; each day he shivered, bearing thorns on his back.
idiomatic: The heir listened to the great villain; each day he shivered, bearing thorns on his back.

idiomatic: Since Eastern Jin's flight from calamity, rites and music have lodged by the Yangzi and Xiang.

literal: Nearly three hundred years have passed since; left lapels have soaked the four quarters.
idiomatic: Nearly three hundred years have passed since; left lapels have soaked the four quarters.

literal: I chant the bitter barbarian and sigh without end; I intone the faint pipes and my grief grows.
idiomatic: I chant the bitter barbarian and sigh without end; I intone the faint pipes and my grief grows.

literal: The Founding Ancestor blazed in his wrath and roused great righteousness at Juzhang.
idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor blazed in his wrath and roused great righteousness at Juzhang.

literal: (At the time he was Jingzhou inspector.)
idiomatic: (At the time he was Jingzhou inspector.)

idiomatic: He handed out rhinoceros cases and crane-knee bows, built Flying Cloud and Warship vessels.

idiomatic: North he raised troops at Han's bend; south he sent grain from Hengyang.

idiomatic: (Xiangzhou inspector Prince of Hedong Yu and Yongzhou inspector Prince of Yueyang Cha both fell under the Jingzhou commandery.)

literal: Long ago the heir of Chenghua attended the emperor; in truth the elder brother died and the younger succeeded.
idiomatic: Long ago the heir of Chenghua attended the emperor; in truth the elder brother died and the younger succeeded.

literal: (When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, the Jin'an king was then made crown prince.)
idiomatic: (When Crown Prince Zhaoming died, the Jin'an king was then made crown prince.)

idiomatic: (The legitimate grandson Huan was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang and died.)

idiomatic: The royal way knew many hardships; each sought his private gain in the capital districts.

idiomatic: Xiangyang blocked its bronze tally; Changsha shut its jade grain.

literal: (Hedong and Yueyang were both sons of Zhaoming.)
idiomatic: (Hedong and Yueyang were both sons of Zhaoming.)

literal: They hastened to fight on their own ground; how could great merit find leisure to gather?
idiomatic: They hastened to fight on their own ground; how could great merit find leisure to gather?

idiomatic: The son had fallen and the nephew attacked; the elder brother was besieged and the uncle struck.

idiomatic: Chu descended the walls by night; Du turned his spears and entered by night.

idiomatic: (Emperor Yuan, because Hedong would not supply ships, sent the heir Fangdeng out as inspector.)

idiomatic: The great army came suddenly; Hedong had no time to send resistance.

idiomatic: The heir trusted petty men, coveted their daughters, jade, and silks, and thus wished to attack them; so Hedong was pressed and fought in rebellion, and the heir was killed by mutinous troops.

idiomatic: Yueyang proclaimed a great hunt and at once led his host to strike Jingzhou, seeking to lift the siege of Xiangzhou.

idiomatic: Chu Xianzu of the Hedong establishment surrendered to Yueyang.

idiomatic: Thus Xiangzhou was taken.

idiomatic: Travelers bent their bows and smiled; flesh and bone slew one another and wept.

idiomatic: Would even the Duke of Zhou still be ill at this? Emperor Wu of Han repented—yet how could he reach it?

idiomatic: When the headquarters' affairs were pressing, I was wrongly chosen from the crowd.

idiomatic: Before the cap was complete I entered office; barely untying my shoes I followed the army.

idiomatic: (At the time he was nineteen; he doffed the hemp and became right regular attendant of the Xiangdong state, and for military merit was added as ink-collar aide of the army pacifying the west.)

idiomatic: When the King of Jing fixed his hegemony, I at last turned shame into a plan for vengeance.

idiomatic: The fleet anchored at Wuchang; the pacifying army garrisoned at Xia'er.

idiomatic: (At the time he sent Xuzhou inspector Xu Wensheng with twenty thousand men to camp at Wuchang's Luzhou to resist Hou Jing's general Ren Yue; his second son Suining duke Fangzhu was made heir, appointed Central Pacifying Army general and Yingzhou inspector, to swell the momentum.)

idiomatic: I was rashly placed among the many talents in the ranks of those joining the army.

idiomatic: (At the time he was transferred to Central Pacifying Army outer-troops aide, in charge of records, and with Wen Pin, Liu Minying, and others kept company with the heir.)

idiomatic: Though the form drew near and the heart was harmonious, it was not what my breast delighted in.

idiomatic: Alas—the noble born in the deep palace; how much more those who lean on the hall and the scale!

idiomatic: He wished to lay bare his heart to stiffen others and set the young teeth ahead to sound first.

idiomatic: (The Central Pacifying Army was then fifteen sui.)

idiomatic: He relied on martial defense in a literary officer,

idiomatic: Wang Ning sat facing the foe; Xiang Xu folded his hands before the troops.

idiomatic: (Ren Yue was pressed by Wensheng; Hou Jing came up himself to rescue him. The ships leaked and were worn; the army was hungry and the soldiers weary; battle after battle was lost.)

idiomatic: He then ordered Song Zixian and Ren Yue to march by land and steal into Yingzhou city; there was no preparation, and so it fell to the bandits.

idiomatic: None failed to change from gibbon to swan and each took his own head to break his skull.
